newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market sees early firm OTC demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market sees early firm OTC demand.

text.p: Buoyant interest in Malaysian issues traded over the counter masked duller demand for blue chips shares in the Singapore stock market early Wednesday.

Dealers said sentiment was mostly mixed on the local front, with some institutional investors buying after a 1.5 percent drop in the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) on Tuesday. But a re-rating of index-linked stocks kept up selling pressure.

"There's some buying back after yesterday's sharp fall but the tendency is to sell down," a dealer with a foreign brokerage said of Tuesday's 32.02 point fall in the STII. At 0220 GMT on Wednesday, the index was up 3.56 points at 2,205.53.
The UOB-OTC index, tracking over the counter trades, rose 6.40 points to 1,365.82 after brushing a new high of 1,366.87.
Some foreign tranches of large STII component stocks clawed back from the week's steep loses. SPH foreign led, up Singapore $0.60 to S$28, and UOB foreign rose S$0.10 to S$16.50.
Malaysian over-the-counter stocks headed the actives list with several pushed to new highs. FACB Berhad traded 16.5 million shares and rose S$0.45 to S$1.03.
Promet Berhad saw 9.26 million shares traded and rose one cent to S$1.72. Insas Berhad was up three cents at S$1.41.
